provision: No more than two-thirds of any elective or appointive body may be of the same gender

source.article: Art. 27(8), Art. 81(b); Art. 261 and Fifth Schedule (five-year legislative deadline); Art. 261(7) (dissolution of Parliament for non-enactment)

text_summary: Art. 27(8): 'the State shall take legislative and other measures to implement the principle that not more than two-thirds of the members of elective or appointive bodies shall be of the same gender.' Art. 81(b) restates it for the electoral system; the Fifth Schedule gave Parliament five years to enact the implementing law, with Art. 261(7) allowing the Chief Justice to advise the President to dissolve Parliament on failure.
period: 2010 to present, but never implemented for Parliament
history: On 11 December 2012 the Supreme Court (Chief Justice Mutunga dissenting) advised that the principle applies to Parliament only 'progressively', with a legislative deadline of 27 August 2015; Parliament extended the deadline by a year and then let five bills fail for lack of quorum. In 2017 the High Court (Mativo J) ruled the failure a 'gross violation' and gave 60 days; nothing followed. On 21 September 2020 Chief Justice Maraga advised President Kenyatta to dissolve Parliament under Art. 261(7); Kenyatta did not act, and on 5 June 2026 a five-judge High Court bench held the advisory itself unconstitutional for procedural reasons. After the 2022 election women held 69 of 349 National Assembly seats (about 20%); President Ruto's campaign promise to deliver the rule within a year is unfulfilled. Devolution to 47 counties under the same constitution, by contrast, was implemented on schedule in 2013.

assessment.reasoning: A clear numerical rule with a deadline and a nuclear sanction has been evaded for sixteen years because the body required to implement it is the body that would lose seats, and the sanction depends on a president who would lose a working Parliament. The devolution provisions in the same text, which created new offices rather than removing them, show that self-interest, not drafting quality, is the variable.

lesson: Never make the enforcement of a representation rule depend on the incumbents it displaces; write the mechanism into the electoral formula itself (reserved or top-up seats) so it executes automatically.
